page: Amazon Web Services c5d.18xlarge is a compute-optimized server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The system is powered by a 3.4 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8124M processor containing 36 physical cores and 72 virtual CPUs with multi-threading enabled. Memory capacity totals 144.0 GB of DDR4 RAM at 3 GHz, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include 1800 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD instance storage, 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and instruction set support for AVX-512 foundation, AES cryptography, and FMA operations. No GPU accelerators are present in this instance type.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core processing and high data throughput capabilities. The server achieves a stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score of 66669.07 and a PassMark CPU score of 49974.67, both placing in the top quartile. Large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 209.03 GB/sec, facilitating high-density data handling. Database benchmarks show elevated efficiency with a PassMark database operations score of 22233.59 and Redis SET operation throughput of 61.64 million operations per second. Conversely, single-threaded processing and small-model LLM text generation metrics reflect average to weak relative standing due to reliance on general CPU execution without hardware accelerators.

The high vCPU density paired with bundled local NVMe storage offers solid qualitative cost efficiency for IO-bound and parallel processing workloads by eliminating external network storage latencies. The instance is suited for batch processing, continuous integration build clusters, distributed database nodes, ETL pipelines, and high-throughput static web serving.
